text: Version 3 is issued in Draft status. No approval of this plan is recorded in this run.
why: The realignment run continues without a human approval gate; a missing approval is recorded rather than waited for.
read: AGENTS.md realignment overlay (D-RCV-60); Template and Rules R1 U8.
confirm: The document owner confirms the plan before it is used as a release gate.
impact: No gate of this plan is treated as signed; the plan is usable for test design.

text: The next version is v3 with date 22 November 2026; the source is v2 of 28 October 2026 even though its document control states Version 1. Version 3 records the source version in a Supersedes row and keeps the source date in section 12.
why: The family version is the file name; the document control row of the source is out of step with it and cannot be copied into a next version unchanged.
read: 09 Testing and quality folder listing (v2 is the highest version of the family); source document control table.
applied_in: Document control table; change log table
confirm: The document owner confirms the version numbering of the family.
impact: A reader of v3 sees both the file version and the version the source states.

text: Every owner in this plan is a service code and short name of the Microservice Ownership Map v1 (P1 to P10, S1 to S9), or a platform epic of Template and Rules R5.1 (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB, RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-DB, RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-EDGE, RWB-PLT-OBS). A team type is written as a role only.
why: The source names teams (QA engineers, SCB IT, ACE team, SCB IT security) and the target needs one owner per test; the Ownership Map is the run's ownership source.
read: Microservice Ownership Map v1, Services sheet; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; Template and Rules R5.1 and R5.3.
applied_in: Sections 3, 6, 7, 8 and 9; Owner rows of every table
confirm: The delivery lead confirms the platform epic codes used for the shared pieces.
impact: Every test has one service or platform owner and no test is owned by a person.

text: The test IDs NFT-<service code>-01 to -05, NFT-J-01 to -12 and NFT-PLT-01 to -08 are new under D-RCV-60 and carry no legacy ID. Numbering runs 01 response time and load, 02 rules and agents, 03 events, workflows and schedules, 04 data, isolation and restore, 05 security, masking and audit.
why: The source has 8 tests and no identifier, so a per-service and journey set needs a new convention to be citable from a story, a defect or a traceability row.
read: Source section 1 table (no ID column); Template and Rules R5.2 (story IDs only) and R7 s16 (test case columns).
confirm: The QA lead confirms the ID convention before test cases are raised against it.
impact: 82 per-service, 12 journey and 8 platform tests become citable; no legacy test case ID is reused.

text: Every pass mark added by this version is copied from section 1 of the source or from Non-functional specification v3, cited by its ID. Where the source has no pass mark (outbox, inbox, retry to .dlt, workflow history, Continue-As-New), the value is taken from Architecture v5 slide 11 and the Temporal and Drools design and named as such.
why: The plan must not set a new target of its own; the target architecture states the mechanisms and their limits, and the test plan applies them.
read: Non-functional specification v3 sections 3.1 to 3.12; Architecture v5 slide 11 and slide 33; Temporal and Drools design (workflow history, Continue-As-New, 300 ms rule, 60 s agent).
confirm: The solution architect confirms the values taken from slide 11 and the Temporal design.
impact: No business value is invented; every figure can be traced to a source line or section.

text: The load of section 1 stays 410 simulated users at three requests a minute for one hour. The other readings of the same figure (370 staff and 50 partner users, 48 concurrent partner users, about 420 concurrent users) are written next to it in section 2 and are not used to change the load.
why: The source load is the value the test was designed on and R3 precedence does not settle which concurrent-user figure is the target; the difference is recorded instead of silently resolved.
read: Source section 1 Load row; Non-functional specification v3 NFR-002 and NFR-003; Architecture v5 slides 33 and 48 notes.
applied_in: Section 2 volume paragraph; section 6.1 load paragraph; section 9 Every wave row
confirm: The solution architect confirms the staff and partner mix of the 410.
impact: The load test keeps a stable figure; a mix change is a small edit to section 2 when confirmed.

text: The pod sizes, the per-service connection caps and the test tools are written with the R9 placeholder. Section 2 states what the target does fix: 19 schemas and logins, one topic and one task queue per service, and an API deployment of 2 pods with KEDA-scaled workers.
why: No source gives a CPU or memory size, a pool cap or a tool name, and a per-service test cannot be sized from a guess.
read: Source section 2; Architecture v5 slides 11, 30 and 33.
confirm: The ACE team and SCB IT set the sizes and the tools before the first per-service test run.
impact: The environment statement is complete on structure and open on size; nothing is invented.

text: The wave of a service is the Wave column of the Microservice Ownership Map v1: P1 to P7, P9 and P10 in wave 1; P8, S2, S5 and S8 in wave 2; S1, S3, S4 and S6 in wave 3; S7 and S9 in wave 4. This matches Architecture v5 slide 38.
why: The source plan orders its tests by release name only and gives no wave per service, while every per-service test needs a gate.
read: Microservice Ownership Map v1, Services sheet; Architecture v5 slide 38; Template and Rules R5.6.
confirm: The delivery lead confirms the wave of each service at release planning.
impact: Each of the 82 per-service tests has a wave and therefore a gate.

text: The accessibility gate 'Each screen' is read as every screen of every service, reached through that service's REST base, and no screen list is added because no source names one.
why: The source gives the gate at screen level and neither the plan nor the architecture inventories screens.
read: Source section 1 Accessibility row; Architecture v5 slides 14 to 20 (tabs of the case record); Ownership Map v1 REST base per service.
applied_in: Section 1 note; section 9 Every screen row
confirm: The business lead confirms the screen list per service when SIT starts.
impact: The gate stays as written; the count of screens is open.

text: The release names E1 to E8 are kept as the source writes them and are read as the eight business epics EP01 to EP08 of the wave map, so a test gated at E5 sits after wave 3 and before wave 4.
why: The source names releases E1 to E8 and no other source in this work package maps them; the eight business epics are the only eight-way split in the run material.
read: Source section 1 When column; Template and Rules R5.6 (wave map EP01 to EP08); Architecture v5 slide 38.
confirm: The delivery lead confirms the release names against the programme plan.
impact: The wave order of section 9 follows; a different reading moves gates, not tests.

text: The 12 journey tests follow the six steps of the recovery journey on Architecture v5 slide 3, the eight routes and the always-on pieces, and name the services that take part in each step; no journey ID is a legacy ID.
why: The source tests the whole system and names no journey, while the target's business value is the journey across 19 services.
read: Architecture v5 slide 3 (journey, eight routes, deviation and decision always on); Ownership Map v1, Workflows and activities and Jobs sheets.
confirm: The business analyst of each epic confirms the steps of its journey.
impact: Each journey test is traceable to a journey step and to the services and workflows behind it.

text: Until NFR-022 and NFR-023 are set under DL11, every restore test runs against the ACE recovery objectives recorded under DL11 and is re-run when a target is set; NFR-071 stays Open under DL27.
why: The source pass mark is the ACE objective and the target has no figure of its own; the test must still gate the first release.
read: Source section 1 Restore row and section 4; Non-functional specification v3 NFR-022, NFR-023 and NFR-071 and its section 5.
confirm: The IT lead with Operational Risk sets NFR-022 and NFR-023.
impact: The restore gate is testable now and is re-run once the objectives exist.

text: No production data is used: synthetic data in DEV and masked copies in SIT and UAT, with party identifiers masked at rest and in use, and no personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs or prompts.
why: The guardrails of the target and NFR-045 and NFR-039 apply to every test in this plan, including the per-service and journey tests.
read: Non-functional specification v3 NFR-039, NFR-040 and NFR-045; Template and Rules R7 s17 guardrails.
confirm: SCB IT security confirms the data used in SIT.
impact: No test row asks for production data.

text: No release date is written by this version. The source date 28 October 2026 is kept, the issue date is 22 November 2026, and any date written into this plan or a later version is tentative.
why: Dates are unchanged and tentative in this run and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: Source document control (Date 28 October 2026); Template and Rules R1 U7 and R8.1 change-log row.
confirm: The delivery lead confirms the programme calendar.
impact: No gate is read as a calendar date.

text: The shared platform tests are owned by platform epics and not by one of the 19 services: gateway-bff by RWB-PLT-EDGE, Kafka by RWB-PLT-EVT, Temporal by RWB-PLT-WF, the schemas and logins by RWB-PLT-DB, observability by RWB-PLT-OBS, and the template, libraries and pipeline by RWB-PLT-TPL and RWB-PLT-LIB.
why: The 8 source tests include pieces that belong to no module, and Template and Rules R5.1 names the seven platform epics that own them.
read: Template and Rules R5.1; Architecture v5 slides 2 and 4; Ownership Map v1 (platform rows for JOB-05, JOB-11, JOB-21 and JOB-22 are PLT).
confirm: The platform team confirms the epic that runs each shared test.
impact: No shared test is orphaned and no service is made accountable for the platform.
